Tax Amounts

Assign reporting categories to reverse-charged tax amounts to organize how these special tax calculations appear in your reports.

When you have reverse charge transactions where the buyer accounts for both the tax liability and the deduction, proper categorization ensures accurate reporting and compliance.

Name
Name

Reporting categories for reverse-charged tax amounts are classification labels that organize the tax calculated on reverse charge transactions for accurate tax reporting.

In reverse charge transactions, the buyer calculates and reports both the output tax (as if they were the seller) and the input tax (as the buyer). While this typically results in a net zero effect, both components must be reported separately for compliance.

Common Reporting Categories

The following categories are commonly used for reverse-charged tax amounts:

• Reverse charge output tax - Tax amounts reported as collected tax

• Reverse charge input tax - Corresponding deductible tax amounts

• Import VAT - Tax on imported goods where reverse charge applies

• Acquisition tax - Tax on intra-community acquisitions

• Services received tax - Tax on services from non-resident suppliers

• Construction sector tax - Reverse charge tax on construction services

• Self-billed tax amounts - Tax on self-billed invoices under reverse charge

Benefits of Using Reporting Categories

Properly categorizing reverse-charged tax amounts provides several advantages:

• Accurate tracking of reverse charge tax liabilities and deductions

• Proper presentation of reverse charge amounts in tax returns

• Clear reconciliation between tax collected and tax deductible on the same transactions

• Compliance with dual reporting requirements for reverse charge mechanisms

• Simplified audit process with properly categorized reverse charge taxes
